Currently, the standard technique for correcting for these movements in cross-matching is limited to using only the available positional data and time information from the different catalogs. This technique has a significant limitation of not accounting for the parallax effect, which means objects at different distances will have different apparent positions even if they are at the same actual position. In our work, we have developed a new method for correcting the movement of objects during cross-matching by also taking into account the parallax effect by using the available photometric data to calculate the distance and use this to correct the position. We have also developed a new algorithm for correcting the movement of objects during cross-matching by also taking into account their proper motion. We have tested our new method by comparing it with the standard method using a set of artificial catalogs with known positions, velocities, and parallaxes, and found that our method is more accurate than the standard method. We have also found that our method is robust to a wide range of errors in the photometric data. The new method has been applied to real data to match the Gaia DR2 catalog with the 2MASS catalog containing photometric information, and we have found that our method has improved the matching to be 10% more accurate than the standard method.

In this paper, a concept of minimal vertex covers is introduced for infinite hypergraphs, and the challenge is raised to determine the minimum size of such covers in every infinite vertex hypergraphs. It is demonstrated that if the hyperedges contain a bounded number of vertices, a vertex cover of minimal size can still be found, although it may not be unique. Furthermore, it is shown that if the hyperedges can have an arbitrarily large number of vertices, a vertex cover of minimal size may not exist, even one that is unique. The study of minimal vertex covers in infinite hypergraphs is continued to explore their characteristic values.

Domain-specific knowledge is frequently captured using comprehensive and structured knowledge graphs or ontologies that detail conceptual relationships. In domains such as medicine and biomedical research, large, complex ontologies hold significant value. Effective visual representations are crucial for navigating and understanding these structures, especially when dealing with vast and interconnected entities. While existing visual tools focus on hierarchical relationships, the management and comprehension of related yet non-connected concepts within large ontologies remain underdeveloped. In response, we introduce OntoPlot, an innovative visualisation system designed to display and facilitate the understanding of unconnected concepts within comprehensive ontologies. By integrating innovative visual connections, OntoPlot enhances user association recognition, streamlining navigation across complex structures. Through the development of a dedicated user interface, OntoPlot enables manual enrichment of unconnected concepts, promoting further knowledge discovery. In addition to serving as a visualisation tool, OntoPlot can be utilised as a knowledge mining platform for discovering unconnected relationships among concepts. As a demonstration of its analytical capabilities, OntoPlot was applied to the SNOMED CT oncology ontology, resulting in the identification of new, relevant unconnected associations that could contribute to ontology enhancements. In conclusion, OntoPlot presents a novel visualisation approach for uncovering and managing unconnected relationships within comprehensive ontologies, further facilitating the discovery of novel associations among related concepts.

For semi-supervised end-to-end automatic speech recognition, we propose combining inter-domain loss methods, specifically inter-model loss and inter-representation loss, in addition to conventional speech-representation based loss techniques. The inter-domain loss techniques are derived from the Task-Cycle loss developed by Chen et al. (2021), and are designed to leverage the knowledge extracted from a well-performing speech model to improve loss optimization. The proposed loss strategy is evaluated on the 960h LibriSpeech corpus and achieves a 4.06% relative improvement in character error rate compared to using only inter-model loss. Notably, when used in conjunction with a recently proposed voice-consonant embedding approach via cycle-consistent adversarial training, as described in Lee et al. (2020), the proposed loss methods demonstrate higher robustness and yields an 8.19% relative improvement over baseline results.

A fundamental theory known as active inference underpins how living beings interact with their surroundings. This theory views the brain as an efficient tool that employs Bayesian principles to create a detailed mental framework, aiming to minimize uncertainty. A predictive coding framework is often utilized in simplified versions of this theory to create models for artificial intelligence systems. Although these systems typically operate in static environments, they are generally designed to avoid obstacles that are temporary in nature. In order to create adaptive navigation systems capable of navigating through dynamic environments, we propose integrating these systems with motor policies that learn from experience. By incorporating uncertainty into these systems, they can initiate their own actions to reduce uncertainty and efficiently complete tasks. We test this idea by developing a deep active inference-based motor skill learning method, which we evaluate using simulated data.

Our study on binary mixtures utilized molecular dynamics simulations to explore the Soret effect resulting from the difference in thermal stability between parallel and antiparallel molecular orientations. In the simulations, the molecules were represented by molecules with two flexible arms that can adopt various spatial configurations. The results indicate that the Soret effect caused by molecular orientation contributes significantly to the thermal stability in both temperature gradient conditions. The thermodynamic property, $\Delta H_t$, exhibits a correlation with the thermal diffusion coefficient, $D_T$, such that their product remains constant across diverse temperature gradients, thus demonstrating the thermodynamic and kinetic equilibrium under isotropic conditions. Conversely, the introduction of molecules with a limited orientation degree of freedom led to a significant decrease in the thermal stability under anisotropic conditions, resulting in a thermodynamic and kinetic imbalance. The proportion of thermodynamic contribution to the thermal stability depends on the flexibility of the molecules' internal degree of freedom, specifically ranging from 50% for rigid molecules to 0% for highly flexible molecules.

The development of Automated Essay Scoring involves a fusion of expertise from Education, Linguistics, and Natural Language Processing. Effective evaluation by an NLP model depends on its ability to identify patterns in written content, even in cases where the writing quality is subpar. Despite the current prominence of large transformer-based models in various NLP applications, these models' computational complexity poses significant practical limitations to their deployment. This research aims to counter this issue by introducing methods to streamline these models for use on a variety of platforms, including mobile devices. To achieve this, we utilize transfer learning, technique selection, and model pruning to create more efficient models. Our study compares the performance of multiple NLP models with varying levels of complexity on an Automated Essay Scoring task, highlighting the potential benefits of using more efficient models, particularly those based on the BERT architecture.

One of the most significant issues in domain adaptive pedestrian detection is the presence of false positives.  To tackle this challenge, our approach targets suppressing false positives without the need for supervision, aligning with typical domain adaptive learning scenarios.  Unlike existing methods that focus on unsupervised clustering for feature learning, we instead take an unsupervised cross-domain clustering approach by utilizing box similarities in both semantic spaces across pedestrian and non-pedestrian boundaries.  Notably, existing clustering-based methods are not directly applicable to this task as they rely on true positives for feature learning.  To address this limitation, we have developed a novel unsupervised negative sample selection method that achieves positive-negative sample balancing for domain adaptive pedestrian detection.  Our approach is built upon a novel re-ranking loss that imposes box-level semantic clustering constraints on negative samples, forcing them to be far away from pedestrian boxes in semantic space.  To achieve this, we have introduced a novel cross-domain loss that measures the distance between positive and negative sample groups in semantic space.  Our approach has been validated on multiple challenging benchmark datasets, achieving a 78.6% false positive suppression rate at a mean average precision of 83.1%, outperforming existing methods with a 6.8% improvement.

This study presents an innovative method for enhancing low-quality music recordings made on consumer-grade devices, which often include distortions like background noise, echo effects, and microphone distortion. A novel deep learning technique combines two processes: a image translation model that removes spatial distortions and a vocoder model that converts linear spectrogram representations into soundwaves, produced through a 3D convolutional approach. To create the vocoder, this research develops a novel dataset comprising music that has been broken down into its distinct frequency ranges, which can be applied to any spectrogram representation. Notably, this enhancement method produces results immediately, without the need for extensive training, making it suitable for real-time applications.

Our primary objective is to comprehensively investigate the impact of a virtual ball's Point of Release on viewers' perception of a throwing motion. Our perceptual study revealed that individuals tend to more readily notice errors in underarm throws where the point of release occurs early, as opposed to late. Conversely, in the case of overarm throws, participants have a greater propensity to identify errors that occur early, as opposed to late. Moreover, variations in the viewer's vantage point and the trajectory of the ball influence the overall perception of realism. These research findings can potentially be applied in the field of computer-generated imagery to enhance the visual authenticity of throwing animations.

To improve decoding efficiency, a novel top-down approach for tree-structured machine translation is introduced, starting with a fully constructed translation tree and gradually refining it from top to bottom. This algorithm can prevent poor predictions in machine translation by ensuring initial low-confidence predictions are later corrected. The decoding process also benefits from incorporating syntactic connections, enabling it to safely explore a smaller search space. The results of our experiments indicate that this algorithm can reduce decoding time by as much as 2.8 times, while achieving similar or improved BLEU scores. Furthermore, our model outperforms the state-of-the-art in machine translation by scoring 16.63 BLEU on the TED multilingual corpus, a significant improvement of 1.13 points.

The credibility of astrochemical simulations largely relies on the accuracy of binding energy values for intermolecular interactions.  In this work, a comprehensive platform is developed to support the use of binding energies in future simulations by providing a reference point for validation and comparison with experimental data.  A collection of intermolecular binding energy values for small molecules and rings is presented along with an evaluation of their reliability, also including an analysis of the variability in binding energies due to differences in quantum chemical methods and basis sets.  A total of 85 gas phase binding energy values were examined with a significant portion being for water, methanol, and ammonia, as well as for the dimers and monomers of water, methanol, formamide, and ammonia.  A discussion on the significance of binding energy discrepancies is also presented including examples of a binding energy discrepancy that could impact the chemical composition of comets.

A multiplicative stochastic process with lognormally distributed lower bounds is studied, where a theoretical model of the process is developed and its distribution, characterized by four parameters, along with its statistical properties, is analytically determined. This model is further validated by demonstrating its compatibility with real-world data through parameter adjustment.

We've devised a novel approach to estimate the expected value of a real-valued function, leveraging random Clifford circuits of minimal depth. By harnessing Shadow Quantum Computing, where traditional computation units are integrated into a quantum system, we demonstrate that deep circuits aren't necessary to attain substantial relative precision in estimation. In particular, our method achieves comparable results with deep circuits of merely eight layers across a range of test functions. Notably, this approach can be implemented using existing hardware, even by those restricted to shallow circuits due to hardware constraints.

The researchers in a particular study extended the solutions found in complex geometric optics to a related system of equations, which was initially investigated in contexts of electrical impedance tomography and the integrable Davey-Stewartson II equations, focusing particularly on the large spectral parameter behavior. They found that the solutions exhibited a novel behavior when the real and imaginary parts of the complex variable z differed significantly. 

In the context of the reference paper by V. A. Galstian, it was observed that the solutions exhibited distinct behaviors depending on whether the solutions were focused more on the x or y axis, due to the presence of two-dimensional currents, which was consistent with the authors' new results. 

Notably, the authors determined the long-distance behavior of certain nonlinear coherent states, which were initially discovered in a different study by A. S. Holevo, focusing particularly on the intrinsic geometric phase, and discovered that the intrinsic geometric phase exhibited a novel property when the real and imaginary parts of the complex variable z differed significantly.

In the context of the integrable Davey-Stewartson II equations, which were initially investigated in a different study by A. S. Holevo, the authors determined the long-distance behavior of the reflection coefficient, which was initially discovered by M. S. Aminov and A. S. Holevo, and discovered that the reflection coefficient exhibited a novel behavior when the real and imaginary parts of the complex variable z differed significantly.

The vast majority of NLP text transformations have inherent limitations in their ability to expand coverage of input data due to the need to preserve the original class label and input-output pairs. In order to overcome this constraint, we propose a concept called sibylvariance, which allows the creation of robust and extensive transformations that can be generated freely. We demonstrate that the sibylvariance concept is applicable to tasks beyond text classification, including instances where the target class label changes and when it remains the same. Building on this concept, we develop sibylvariant transformations that can be used in scenarios such as semantic text similarity, where the target class label changes and a predictable output is expected. We also provide guidance on the effective utilization of these transformations to improve robustness in text classification.

Researchers aim to create meta-learning algorithms that capitalize on previous experience to rapidly acquire new skills or adapt to new environments by utilizing representation learning techniques, which enable the transfer of knowledge across various tasks. As the interest in meta-learning grows, there is a pressing need to establish its theoretical foundations, particularly in terms of learning adaptable representations. In this research, we tackle the problem of multi-task linear regression where multiple related tasks share a common, low-dimensional linear representation. Our study provides effective, sample-efficient methods to address the dual challenges of learning a shared feature set from related tasks and transferring this knowledge to unseen tasks. This work sheds light on the central issue of meta-learning.

Researchers have successfully applied model compression and knowledge distillation techniques to create efficient yet effective multilingual and low-resource machine translation models. Although these methods can substantially reduce model sizes, their effectiveness in real-world settings is uncertain due to the lack of studies on their reliability in translating sequences of text. We analyzed the robustness and stability of compression and distillation techniques in model-based low-resource MT settings, using a variety of evaluation metrics that measure translation quality, divergence from the original model, and task-specific metrics. We tested six model compression methods, along with a knowledge distillation approach, in a MT setting for the Swahili English task, and discovered that the majority of compression methods failed to produce stable translations. Notably, our findings suggest that the top-performing distillation model outperformed all compression models in our study, and we propose that distillation is a more suitable approach than compression for building low-resource MT models due to its relative stability.

The Turan number for an r-uniform graph F, denoted by ex(n, F), is defined as the maximum number of edges in an F-free r-uniform graph on n vertices. The Turan density of F, denoted by pi(F), is defined as the limit of the maximum number of edges over the total possible number of edges as the vertex number approaches infinity. The author shows that for a specific 3-uniform graph, known as the claw, that there does not exist a computable rational number representing its Turan density, meaning that there is no finite rational number that can approximate pi(F) in a computable way, within any positive error margin.

The goal of semantic segmentation in medical imaging is to identify the class of each pixel, which is particularly challenging when dealing with rare conditions due to the limited availability of labelled data. In this study, we investigate how different image augmentation techniques can help alleviate the scarcity of labelled data for a specific task, namely the segmentation of lung lesions in chest X-rays to detect pneumonia. Utilizing state-of-the-art deep learning models on a simulated dataset generated by image augmentation techniques, we demonstrate that combining two types of augmentations, demosaicking and interpolation, with a moderate level of application can match the performance of models trained with double the labelled data on the task of lesion segmentation. Furthermore, our results suggest that these augmentations also improve the accuracy of classification for pneumonia. It is anticipated that the detected patterns in our study will be generalizable to other rare medical image analysis tasks.

Existing image captioning models often fail to produce captions according to specific requirements due to their large model sizes and limits on processing arbitrary input sequences. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel image captioning model called I3P, which utilizes prompt-based learning to CAPturate precise DEScriptions. I3P features a tiny encoder that can handle images of any resolution, a set of reusable natural language prompts that expand the vocabulary limits, and a transformer decoder with a few layers. Notably, I3P's primary components resemble those of text generation models, allowing it to produce captions for images and process prompts efficiently. We demonstrate I3P's superiority by evaluating it on fluency, coherence, and text-based metrics and comparing it to leading image captioning models. Additionally, we showcase I3P's capabilities in producing diverse, tag-based, and controllable captions.

The concept of harm has been difficult to pin down due to its various forms, and previous attempts to analyze it have been hindered by non-causal accounts. This paper argues that only adverse causal consequences accurately capture the essence of harm, and it offers a precise definition of harm as the increase in an agent's undesirable causal outcomes. This definition's precision stems from a prior development in modal logic that enables the quantification of the best causal outcomes an agent can achieve. Utilizing this definition, the paper draws a distinction between active and passive harm, and it demonstrates how to calculate the level of harm experienced by a passive victim. Moreover, the paper proposes a new concept, beneficial risk, which emerges from the harm framework, and it illustrates its significance through its distinction from mere risk.

This study showcases MMLSpark, an innovative open-source library that bridges the gap between Cognitive Toolkit and Apache Spark, enabling seamless integration with open-source deep learning tools. By utilizing MMLSpark, users can access a wide range of sophisticated Spark extensions for data preparation, model training, and analysis, thus streamlining the machine learning and data science processes. The paper highlights the benefits of MMLSpark's scalable architecture and highlights three core applications: efficient handling of irregular data, complex data transformations, and advanced model training.

Speech-to-text translation involves converting spoken language into written language across different tongues. Conventional two-stage approaches using speech recognition and machine translation have limitations, as they can't seamlessly convey cultural nuances like idioms or maintain the original's tone or intent. We introduce a zero-shot speech translation model that directly converts spoken audio into written text in a foreign language, bypassing intermediate speech transcription. This model leverages large-scale datasets, including audio samples in one language and written examples in another, to learn patterns and relationships between spoken words and their written equivalents. During testing, it can translate spoken audio into written text it's never seen before, all without needing transcribed speech data as an intermediate step. We demonstrate that this approach can achieve speech translation results on par with known baselines on Romanian-English and Mandarin-English datasets, while also improving translation quality on English-Romanian tasks by tackling idioms and tone.

This work introduces a novel extension to the traditional heat conduction theory, encompassing cases with dynamic boundary conditions. In doing so, it is established that the thermal energy's balance principle remains unaltered, while the related boundary equation $\partial_\tau q|_{\partial\Omega}=\beta \partial_\tau h|_{\partial\Omega}$, along with the boundary condition $h|_{\partial\Omega}=g$, is subject to the modified boundary principle of energy. This expanded model incorporates elements of standard heat conduction, the Guyer and Grant equation, the Maxwell-Cattaneo equation, and the extended Maxwell-Cattaneo model. In addition, it is observed that the extended Maxwell-Cattaneo model is a limiting case of the non-linear Guyer and Grant equation when the relaxation time tends towards zero.

Precise short-term forecasts of energy consumption are essential for managing the low voltage electricity network efficiently, particularly with regard to highly disaggregated load distributions among a small number of customers. While individual customer load forecasts are subject to significant uncertainty, the aggregate load of a small number of customers provides a more reliable forecast. This increased reliability is due to the canceling out of uncertain load components among the customers. This work investigates the benefits of combining forecasts of aggregate and individual loads to reduce uncertainty. By fusing probabilistic forecasts, the error is expected to cancel out, resulting in an improved forecast accuracy. The study compares linear and non-linear aggregation methods and finds that the fusion of forecasts can reduce the error by up to 40m^2 (standard deviations) for peak load predictions. The impact of weather on load forecasts is also significant, particularly during peak hours, and including a bias correction can further enhance forecast accuracy.

The growth of machine learning algorithms has not entirely resolved the issues affecting AI performance, primarily due to limited data and insufficient resources. However, augmenting a model with relevant information can address some of these challenges to a degree. This paper explores the ways in which domain expertise can be integrated into machine learning for improved performance. We categorize knowledge integration methods into information access and representation approaches. Starting with data-related strategies such as selective data collection and post-processing, the methodologies progress to labeling and sequencing techniques. Moving to model representation, we discuss how knowledge can be embedded in a model's structure or utilized in inference as an add-on. We examine various knowledge representation formats, including graphs and rules, and consider the challenges associated with each format. This survey aims to provide an extensive review of knowledge integration methods, highlighting their benefits and drawbacks, as well as addressing common evaluation metrics and performance measurement challenges.

Creating a reliable model for precise COVID-19 detection on chest CT scans poses significant difficulties despite considerable advancements. The issue often arises due to annotation biases affecting traditional supervised segmentation techniques, which rely on precise pixel-level markings. These limitations can result in models that identify distinct features of normal tissue and COVID-19 lesions, known as mode dropping, leading to inaccurate predictions and failure to generalize to unseen data. In this context, we have developed a novel approach to COVID-19 detection that utilizes weakly supervised learning, allowing us to train our model using image-level labels, thus alleviating the need for precise pixel-level annotations. By combining WSLS with a novel objective function, our method promotes the identification of COVID-19 lesions with greater consistency and accuracy, ultimately enhancing COVID-19 detection performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art methods, achieving an AP of 67.44%, along with an average AP of 66.25% and 65.58% for class-specific AP calculation, for lesion detection and COVID-19 detection, respectively.

Accurate vertebrae localization and identification are crucial in various medical applications related to spine disorders. We introduce a novel method using a prior vertebral model to generate candidate vertebrae, and then employ anatomically-constrained optimization to identify the optimal vertebrae. To facilitate efficient optimization, the initial candidate vertebrae are aligned in the anterior direction. We also introduce a vertebral detection network to provide an initial estimation of the identity loss, and integrate it with the optimization process. The proposed method has been extensively validated through experiments on publicly available datasets and has achieved state-of-the-art performance. Notably, our approach outperforms existing methods by 5% in terms of the mean detection rate for individual vertebrae.

Our study presents a theory on stabilizing molecules using anti-correlated strong photon field fluctuations arising from the vacuum, in an attempt to apply resonant electron-molecule scattering to the ultrastrong light-matter coupling regime. We suggest a feasible experimental approach to generate the anti-photonic field through the interaction of molecules and a one-dimensional photonic crystal cavity. We also provide estimates for the necessary coupling strength and stability period based on calculations involving CO molecules.

In the field of legged locomotion, spring-based actuators can boost energy efficiency and performance but complicate the controller's design. We diverge from conventional methods that treat these actuators as established components and instead educate our controller to utilize their elastic features. A novel control approach rooted in model-predictive control not only considers optimal reference trajectories but also optimizes these actuators' characteristics under given constraints. By leveraging this framework, our method significantly reduces the controller's complexity caused by elastic actuators. We test our approach on a quadruped robot equipped with series-series elastic actuators and compare its performance to a traditional constant-gain feedback controller. Our results indicate that our model-predictive control approach can enhance movement speed, decrease fuel consumption, and enable the elastic actuators' effective utilization.

Quantum systems in separable states exhibit distinct subspaces, and the task is to determine if a given mixed state remains separable across different subspaces. Various methods have been developed to solve the quantum separability problem, but the application of these methods is limited due to their distinct workloads: some are efficient in handling separability problems with low dimensions, others in dealing with rank problems, and yet others in handling both. As a result, there is a need for a new approach that can efficiently handle separability problems with both low dimensions and ranks. A new algorithmic paradigm has been proposed to solve the quantum separability problem, and the method has been tested on known bilinear families of separable states, and has successfully identified all non-orthogonal maximally entangled states of low dimensions. Additionally, the method has been applied to rank-one decomposable states, and has confirmed the known results on their bilinear families.

Electrostatic simulations have uncovered a previously unobserved, drive-independent, elliptical instability in collisionless slab plasmas. This instability manifests as a small-scale tearing mode, characterized by a magnetic field structure resembling an electron filament. Unlike its electrodynamic counterpart, the drive-independent nature of this instability is attributed to electron temperature fluctuations. In the electron fluid model, these fluctuations result in electron density perturbations that are simultaneously constrained by the electron dispersion relation and the magnetic field topology. In the electrostatic limit, these perturbations grow exponentially due to electron heating, giving rise to the small-scale tearing mode. In contrast to the electrodynamic case, the drive-dependent nature of this instability is attributed to electron temperature fluctuations. In the electrostatic limit, these perturbations result in electron density and magnetic field coupling, leading to a modified electron distribution that can drive a small-scale electrodynamic instability. In the electrodynamic limit, these perturbations result in a modified electron temperature and density distribution that can drive a small-scale electrostatic instability.

A novel approach of semi-supervised feature-level attribute manipulation has been proposed for fashion images, addressing the challenge of retrieving real-world images based on a mixture of style and attribute preferences. The inherent ambiguity in fashion leads to conflicting styles and attributes in desired results, often requiring images to combine contrasting features such as formalality, color, texture, and accessories. Existing methods fall short by assuming a single label per image, neglecting the complexity of style and attribute interactions. To overcome these limitations, a semi-supervised attribute manipulation approach has been developed to iteratively refine pre-trained features, effectively improving the performance of fashion image retrieval. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art results on the Zappos-style dataset, achieving a top-ranked retrieval rate of 82.0% with attribute manipulation, while showcasing generalization capabilities to real-world image retrieval tasks.

The $\R$-optimal solution for the underdetermined equation $Ax=y$ where $A$ is a bounded linear operator mapping a Banach space to a Hilbert space, and $\R$ is a strongly convex function defined in that space, is investigated. A dual gradient flow is proposed to find this solution, and convergence is demonstrated for any initial condition under the condition that the gradient flow remains in a strictly convex, finite-valued function. Furthermore, this approach is applied to compute computed tomography, and a numerical example is presented to illustrate its feasibility.

Constructing the matching cost is a vital component in estimating light field depth, and current cost construction methods are generally inefficient as they fail to account for occlusions and selectively sample pixels from different viewing angles, leading to suboptimal performance. In response to these limitations, we have developed a pioneering occlusion-aware cost constructor specifically designed for light field depth estimation, which effectively detects occlusions and calculates a cost metric tailored to non-occluded pixels sampled from multiple viewing angles through a novel epipolar flow approach. As a result, our constructor outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin on benchmark datasets, and the source code is freely available for public use.

This study uses the bilinear method to investigate the Fokas-Lenells equations, first reducing the system and then employing the Jacobi elliptic perturbation technique to derive novel solutions. The Fokas-Lenells equations are viewed as a bridge between the nonlinear Schrödinger equation and the NLS-type elliptic equation, allowing for a comparison of solutions obtained via the bilinear method and those from the known Mikelesen-Oikawa-Yajima transformation for NLS.

Alternative theories of gravity that go beyond the Riemannian formula are explored in a framework called double field theory. Torsion is incorporated into the gravitational action by using the $f$-scalar curvature from Torsion-Scalable Gravity, which is then applied to various modified gravity theories. The supergravity nature of these modifications is confirmed when their corresponding Torsion-Scalable counterparts exhibit supergravity properties. The supergravity properties in these modifications arise from the non-geometric torsion terms in the gravitational action. Theorems demonstrating the supergravity properties in these modifications are formulated and exemplified through several case studies. The theorems cover three types of supergravity properties: $\mathcal{N}=1$, $\mathcal{N}=2$, and $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric, depending on the gravity theory and Bianchi identities satisfied. The study also includes a new type of supergravity solution for $f(\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{X})$-modified Palatini gravity that is distinct from the known solutions in literature and does not require Palatini variation.

To meet growing demand for home WiFi networks, many users set up additional access points as backup devices, which are strategically located to provide coverage where it's needed most. However, these devices, also known as extenders, can often be mistaken for regular access points by devices in the network, which can lead to subpar performance. In this context, a novel approach is proposed to optimize home WiFi networks by utilizing tools from the IEEE 802.11k/v standard to make informed decisions about which access points are best suited to serve specific clients. By leveraging these standards, it's possible to consider the spatial distribution of access points and devices in the network, as well as the channels they're using, to minimize interference and ensure a stronger signal. Our approach takes into account the capabilities of each access point, including its range, speed, and compatibility with other devices in the network, to make informed decisions about which devices should communicate with which access points, ultimately improving overall network performance. By using these tools, it's possible to provide a better user experience, especially for applications that require a high amount of data, such as online gaming and streaming, without the need for a more complex network architecture.
